category_title: Verbal students with Asperger syndrome who engage in monologues and have visual impairments
minimal_context: Kaylie is participating in a 5-minute conversational interaction session with a peer without disabilities using a Braille communication book.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Kaylie, it is time for your 5-minute conversation session with your peer partner. Please use your Braille communication book to start.

STUDENT: (Rubs her eyes) When I meet new people I’m sort of nervous.

TUTOR: Just try your best to pick a topic from the book.

STUDENT: (Speaks in a continuous monologue without pausing) I listened to a new audio book yesterday about horses and there are so many different breeds of horses, some are very tall and some are small, and I think the small ones are interesting but the tall ones run faster and I want to learn more about them...

TUTOR: Kaylie, you need to make a decision on which question to ask your partner now.

STUDENT: (Begins rubbing her face and smelling the edge of the communication book) Well, I don’t know what I want! I never have enough time!

options.A: Provide the peer partner with a brief description of the student's conversation style (e.g., "Kaylie has a visual impairment so she reads Braille").
options.B: Use psychometric assessments to set individual conversational targets for the student and provide frequent acknowledgment of her achievements during the sessions.
options.C: Use learning analytics for the early identification of at-risk students prior to scheduling the 5-minute conversational interaction sessions with peers.
options.D: Ensure the student and the peer partner do not arrive late or leave early during the scheduled 5-minute conversational interaction sessions.
